text: Definition 1 (Practical and standard Newton–Schulz polynomials). The practical NS polynomial is $p_{\mathrm{P}}(x)=a_{\mathrm{P}}+b_{\mathrm{P}}x+c_{\mathrm{P}}x^{2},\qquad(a_{\mathrm{P}},b_{\mathrm{P}},c_{\mathrm{P}})=(3.4445,-4.7750,2.0315).$ For $k\in\mathbb{N}$ , the degree- $k$ standard NS polynomial is the Taylor polynomial of $x^{-1/2}$ at $x=1$ : $p_{\mathrm{S}}^{(k)}(x)=\sum\nolimits_{\ell=0}^{k}\frac{(2\ell)!}{4^{\ell}(\ell!)^{2}}(1-x)^{\ell}.$ In particular, $p_{\mathrm{S}}^{(2)}(x)=a_{\mathrm{S}}+b_{\mathrm{S}}x+c_{\mathrm{S}}x^{2}$ with $(a_{\mathrm{S}},b_{\mathrm{S}},c_{\mathrm{S}})=(15/8,-5/4,3/8).$
Assumption 1 (Low boundedness). The objective satisfies $f_{\inf}=\inf_{W\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}}f(W)>-\infty.$
Assumption 2 (Smoothness). There exists a constant $L>0$ such that, for all $X,Y\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ , $\|\nabla f(X)-\nabla f(Y)\|_{F}\leq L\|X-Y\|_{F}.$

Theorem 1 (NS with WD). Under Assumptions 1 – 3 , consider the iterates of Algorithm 1 with $\eta=\frac{c_{1}}{T^{3/4}},~1-\beta=\frac{c_{2}}{T^{1/2}},~\varepsilon\in\left(0,\frac{c_{3}}{T^{1/4}}\right],~\lambda=\frac{C_{2}}{2\bigl(\left\lVert W_{0}\right\rVert_{F}+C_{3}c_{1}T^{1/4}\bigr)},~T\geq\max\{1,c_{2}^{2}\},$ (8) where $c_{1},c_{2},c_{3}$ are $\mathcal{O}(1)$ constants defined in ( 20 ), and $C_{3}$ is an $\mathcal{O}(1)$ constant defined in ( 11 ). Then $\displaystyle\frac{1}{T}\sum\nolimits_{t=0}^{T-1}\mathbb{E}\left\lVert\nabla f(W_{t})\right\rVert_{F}=\mathcal{O}\Big(\frac{\sqrt[4]{L(f(W_{0})-f_{\inf})\sigma^{2}/b_{\mathrm{mb}}}}{{T^{1/4}}}\Big).$ (9)

Corollary 1 (NS without WD). Under Assumptions 1 – 3 , consider the iterates of Algorithm 1 with $\eta=\frac{c_{1}}{T^{3/4}},\quad 1-\beta=\frac{c_{2}}{T^{1/2}},\quad\varepsilon\in\left(0,\frac{c_{3}}{T^{1/4}}\right],\quad\lambda=0,\quad T\geq\max\{1,c_{2}^{2}\},$ where $c_{1},c_{2},c_{3}$ are defined in ( 20 ) with $(C_{2}/2+C_{3})$ replaced by $C_{3}$ . Then $\frac{1}{T}\sum\nolimits_{t=0}^{T-1}\mathbb{E}\left\lVert\nabla f(W_{t})\right\rVert_{F}=\mathcal{O}\Big(\frac{\sqrt[4]{L(f(W_{0})-f_{\inf})\sigma^{2}/b_{\mathrm{mb}}}}{{T^{1/4}}}\Big).$ (10)

Proposition 2 (Ill-conditioned quadratic). Let $h,\ell,\kappa\in\mathbb{N}$ , with $\kappa\gg 1$ , $\ell=h\kappa$ , $r=h+\ell$ . Define $Q=\operatorname{diag}(\kappa I_{h},I_{\ell}),\qquad f(W)=\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{tr}(W^{\top}QW),\qquad W_{0}=I_{r}.$ The high-curvature block accounts for most of the gradient energy, while each block contributes half of the objective value. We consider practical NS or standard NS with $k=2$ , and normalize without an $\varepsilon$ -stabilizer, stopping when the gradient vanishes. (i) One-step contraction. Denote $\tau_{0}\hskip-1.00006pt=\hskip-1.00006pt\left\lVert\nabla f(W_{0})\hskip-1.00006pt\right\rVert_{F}=\hskip-1.00006pt\sqrt{h\kappa(\kappa+1)},~u=q_{5}(\kappa/\tau_{0}),~v=q_{5}(1/\tau_{0}).$ For deterministic Muon without momentum or WD, the respective optimal stepsizes minimizing $f(W_{1})$ for the two NS choices yield $\frac{f(W_{1})}{f(W_{0})}=\frac{h\kappa\ell(u-v)^{2}}{(h\kappa+\ell)(h\kappa u^{2}+\ell v^{2})}=\frac{(u-v)^{2}}{2(u^{2}+v^{2})}\leq\left(\frac{u-v}{u+v}\right)^{2}.$ Consider the example with $h=1$ and $\ell=\kappa=100$ , five practical and standard NS iterations give $(u,v)\approx(0.7020,0.6968)$ and $(1,0.2274)$ , respectively, leaving $0.0014\%$ and $28.3789\%$ of $f(W_{0})$ after the one-step update. For fixed $h$ and $\kappa\to\infty$ , substituting $u=q_{5}(1/\sqrt{h})+\mathcal{O}(\kappa^{-1})$ and $v=a^{5}/(\kappa\sqrt{h})+\mathcal{O}(\kappa^{-2})$ gives $\frac{f(W_{1})}{f(W_{0})}=\frac{1}{2}-\frac{a^{5}}{\kappa\sqrt{h}\,q_{5}(1/\sqrt{h})}+\mathcal{O}(\kappa^{-2}).$ When $q_{5}(1/\sqrt{h})$ is close to one for both NS choices, the leading-order improvement is mainly governed by $a^{5}$ , which is approximately $484.8762$ for practical NS and $23.1743$ for standard NS. Thus, practical NS yields a substantially stronger one-step contraction. (ii) Full optimization trajectory. Consider the example with $h=1$ and $\ell=\kappa=100$ . Let $W_{t}^{\mathrm{P}}$ and $W_{t}^{\mathrm{S}}$ denote the Muon iterates generated by practical and standard NS, respectively, using the optimal stepsizes at each iteration $t$ that minimize $f(W_{t+1}^{\mathrm{P}})$ and $f(W_{t+1}^{\mathrm{S}})$ . Then $\frac{f(W_{t}^{\mathrm{P}})}{f(W_{0})}\leq(6.4514\times 10^{-5})^{t},\qquad\frac{f(W_{t}^{\mathrm{S}})}{f(W_{0})}\geq(0.1406)^{t}.$ Further comparisons for different values of $h$ and $\kappa$ are provided in Table 2 . Lemma 2 0 (NS direction alignment). For both practical and standard NS, the momentum $M_{t}$ and the resulting direction $D_{t}$ in Algorithm 1 satisfy $\displaystyle\langle M_{t},D_{t}\rangle_{F}\geq C_{2}\left\lVert M_{t}\right\rVert_{F}-C_{2}\varepsilon/4,\qquad\left\lVert D_{t}\right\rVert_{F}\leq C_{3},$ where $C_{2}\hskip-1.00006pt=\hskip-1.00006pt\min_{s\in[0,1]}\chi_{5}(s)\hskip-1.00006pt>\hskip-1.00006pt0,~C_{1}\hskip-1.00006pt=\hskip-1.00006pt\max_{s\in[0,1]}\chi_{5}(s)\hskip-1.00006pt>\hskip-1.00006pt0$ , as defined above, and $\displaystyle C_{3}=\min\{C_{1},q_{\max}\sqrt{r}\},\qquad q_{\max}=\max\nolimits_{s\in[0,1]}q_{5}(s),\qquad r=\min\{m,n\}.$ In particular, $(C_{2},C_{1},q_{\max})=\begin{cases}(0.6964\ldots,\,484.8762\ldots,\,1.2023\ldots),&\text{practical NS},\\ (1,\,a^{5},\,1),&\text{standard NS}.\end{cases}$
